item.title: The $280 Billion Chinese Outbound Comeback That Destinations Can’t Ignore
item.description: The China rebound won’t reward destinations that advertise the loudest. It will reward those that make travel easiest, be it with visas, payments or logistics. Clarity will now sell more than landmarks.

item.title: The Great British Airline Loyalty Battle
item.description: As many British Airways flyers brace for status downgrades, rivals are seizing a rare chance to convince the UK’s most valuable travelers that there’s another way.

item.title: Why Misjudging African Tourism Risk Is a Billion-Dollar Mistake
item.description: Africa’s tourism outlook is improving as air access and traveler interest continue to expand. For investors and global travel brands, the question is no longer whether the sector can deploy capital effectively, but whether delay itself now carries the greater risk.

item.title: Aviation’s Next Green Fuel Problem: Can Europe’s eSAF Mandate Survive?
item.description: The race is on to prove eSAF supply can catch up with Europe’s mandates. But with plants taking four years to build, policymakers may have to consider adjusting their targets.

item.title: Spirit Airlines Reaches Deal With Creditors to Emerge From Chapter 11 Bankruptcy
item.description: Spirit is set to emerge from its second Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the late spring or early summer. Post-bankruptcy, it is looking to expand premium seats and shift focus to routes with high-demand.

item.title: Kayak’s New Ad Campaign Signals a Marketing Dilemma as AI Grabs Share
item.description: Booking Holdings sees AI as the future of travel. Its Kayak brand's marketing doesn't touch on AI, but is trying to convince Millennials it's OK to book on smartphones and to use Kayak to navigate social media distractions.

item.title: Starwood Hotels’ CEO on Why the Revived Brand Is Staying Small
item.description: The original Starwood Hotels became a powerhouse through a scale game. The revived brand name is a bet that less can be more in today's world of digital distribution and marketing.

item.title: Why a U.S.-Based Luxury Safari Company Is Suddenly Courting Indian Travelers
item.description: Micato Safaris supported India's inbound potential much before it saw a market where it can sell its luxury offerings. But now, it is time to change the strategy.

item.title: S4BT Acquires Business Travel Hotel-Booking Platform
item.description: S4BT has acquired HotelHub, bringing $5 billion in annual corporate hotel bookings into its network. The deal gives the group a much bigger role in how business travelers book hotels, without turning it into a traditional travel agency.

item.title: Why India’s Travel Market is at a Critical Inflection Point
item.description: India’s travel economy is loud, liquid, and expanding. But scratch the surface, and the contradictions get uncomfortable.
